questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The courses available, how good at english they were in host country, how organised they seemed both online and via e-mail.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, Vrije Universiteit did a lot to make everything easy to figure out, and they very quick to respond over e-mail - super helpful!

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: They helped a lot with practical matters in the the intro week; registering with the municipality, signing Erasmus papers, housing, where to find help etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found housing through the university, so it was easy, the apartment was just not located on campus.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
I think I found the best housing out of everyone I knew on exchange. I lived in Cornelis Lelylaan and it was the perfect location. 15 minutes on bike to campus, 15 mins on bike to the city center, and it had all types of transport 1 minute away from my building; trams, metro, trains, busses. The Sprinter train to the airport took only 5 minutes. Also the area was safe, and the bike ride to uni was really nice and scenic. 
Also I had my own apartment to myself, which was really nice, but also meant that I could get housing allowance, which halfed my monthly rent, so I ended up paying the least rent out of everyone I knew in Amsterdam, including those living in shared housing (with 10 roommates).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I think I found the best housing out of everyone I knew on exchange. I lived in Cornelis Lelylaan and it was the perfect location. 15 minutes on bike to campus, 15 mins on bike to the city center, and it had all types of transport 1 minute away from my building; trams, metro, trains, busses. The Sprinter train to the airport took only 5 minutes. Also the area was safe, and the bike ride to uni was really nice and scenic. 
Also I had my own apartment to myself, which was really nice, but also meant that I could get housing allowance, which halfed my monthly rent, so I ended up paying the least rent out of everyone I knew in Amsterdam, including those living in shared housing (with 10 roommates). 
I can really recommend Cornelis Lelylaan, it was the perfect location, an all new building (everything worked perfectly), and the cheapest out of all the options.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found it very easy, the only downside was that course registration was quite close to my departure which was a little stressfull. I was not sure if I was going to get the courses I needed until 2 weeks before I left.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: So many steps, so many things to fill out and upload. It felt like a part-time job. But in the end I think that its just the exchange experience, and what everyone probably goes through.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I could e-mail my host and sending universities (which I did a lot), and also some information was available online.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful, I got all of the courses I needed and wanted. And I found out immediately when i registered for them, which was super nice - no waiting time at VU.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Even though they open course registration quite late, in my experience, everyone got the courses they wanted, so be patient and know that it will all sort itself out. 
Also send e-mails to the incoming team, research yourself online on their website. They had quite a lot of information there aswell. They also had a webinar on the course registration which was super helpful.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found the courses to be interesting, but also super hard. There is a lot more homework, group work and weekly tests, that I am not used to at my home university. I spent a lot more time on uni during my exchange than I have done at my home university.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I found the courses to be super hard. Prepare yourself for a lot of work. There is a lot more homework, assignments, group work and weekly tests, that I am not used to at my home university. I spent a lot more time on uni during my exchange than I have done at my home university.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: much more group work, more "homework", more assignments, less lectures and more class. But I did have fewer lectures/classes overall compared to my home university, meaning that I had to be at uni less than I am used to.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Current Topics in Cognition, Evolutionary Psychology, Research Toolbox, Identity, Diversity and Inclusion & Group Dynamics.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Evolutionary Psychology and Research Toolbox were the least work out of all of the courses I had, and Current Topics in Cognition and Identity, Diversity and inclusion were the most work out of all of the courses I had. Groups Dynamics was in between. 
I mostly enjoyed the course Identity, Diversity and Inclusion even though it was a bit more work. It was super interesting and the lecturer was really good.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: There is a mandatory garbage and water bill, which are a bit expensive. I think the garbage bill (for the 6 months) was around 1000 DKK and the water bill was around 650 DKK.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Going out is a bit cheaper than in Denmark, eating at restaurants and going to bars costs less money. Groceries are more expensive than in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not participate in any, but a lot of friends did. There is both a cheap gym at uni you can join, dancing classes, volleyball, rowing, a choir etc. They had so many activities.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: So many! Both clubs, sports, support groups etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Get a bike and bike around, its so easy and really nice to bike near the water. Also theres a really nice study cafe called NIO, that i wish I had found earlier than I did.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Do a boat tour, do the Heineken Experience, bike through Vondelpark, see the Highland Cows in Amsterdamse Bos, go to Papeneiland for the famous apple tart. There are also so many nice cafes, restaurants bars. Especially in the areas Joordan and Bilderdijkstraat. 
Do day trips - my favorites were: Utrecht, Haag, Leiden, Zaandam.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Amsterdam is very similar to Copenhagen. The Dutch people are great at english and super nice. The exchange students are all looking to make friends, so they are also super friendly and open.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Go to the ESN events. There are so many espescially in the beginning. They do bar crawls, kaaroke night, city tour etc. and its very cheap to participate. 
Also the intro week hosted by the university is where I met all of my friends, so I would really recommend that you participate in that. Its one full week with a lot of different opportunities to meet people.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing really.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The biking

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
You will find housing. Everyone I know on exchange in Amsterdam got housing through the university. Dont worry. 
You will get the courses that you need, even if it is last minute. 
Amsterdam is such a lovely city, get a bike and drive around. Its the easiest way to get around.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I really recommend living in the Cornelis Lelylaan building near Lelylaan station. It was a perfect location.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Finding friends from all over the world. Learning many new things about different countries and cultures. Living and becoming familiar with Amsterdam.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The courses and the amount of work I spend on uni. I had not expected that.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
